bouillon de boeuf, déshydraté.note: Ready-to-use beef stock can replace dehydrated stock (reconstitute according to the dosage).

levure de bière en paillettes.note: Brewer's yeast flakes can be swapped for standard brewer's yeast.

levure de boulanger fraîche.note: Dried baker's yeast can replace fresh yeast (about half the weight).

levure de boulanger déshydratée.note: Fresh baker's yeast can replace dried yeast (about double the weight).

vanille, extrait alcoolique.note: A scraped vanilla pod can replace alcohol-based vanilla extract.

fond de veau pour sauces et cuisson, dés.note: Ready-to-use veal stock can replace dehydrated stock (reconstitute according to the dosage).

court-bouillon pour poissons, déshydraté.note: Ready-to-use fish stock is a good alternative to dehydrated court-bouillon.

extrait de levure, à tartiner.note: Soy sauce brings a similar umami note and can replace spreadable yeast extract in cooking.

gélifiant pour confitures.note: Pectin is a classic substitute for jam-setting gelling agent.

vanille, gousse.note: Vanilla extract (about 1 tsp) can replace a vanilla pod.

menthe, séchée.note: Fresh mint can replace dried mint (triple the amount).

romarin, séché.note: Fresh rosemary can replace dried rosemary (triple the amount).

sauge, séchée.note: Fresh sage can replace dried sage (triple the amount).

estragon, séché.note: Fresh tarragon can replace dried tarragon (triple the amount).

aneth, séché.note: Fresh dill can replace dried dill (triple the amount).

ciboulette, séchée.note: Fresh chives can replace dried chives (triple the amount).

préparation culinaire à base de soja, ty.note: A classic plant-based alternative to crème fraîche in cooking (dishes, sauces).

tofu nature, préemballé.note: Plain tofu is a common plant-based substitute for chicken breast in stir-fries and curries.

seitan, préemballé.note: Seitan is a common plant-based substitute for ground beef in stews and bolognese dishes.

caviar de tomates.note: A similar vegetable-based spread, interchangeable with eggplant caviar for appetizers.

huile de macadamia.note: Mild, neutral-tasting oil with a similarly high smoke point; good substitute for both cooking and dressing.

huile de périlla.note: Regular sesame oil, less pronounced flavor but same Asian character; works in Korean/Japanese dishes.

huile de palme rouge, non raffinée.note: Refined palm oil, less intense color and flavor (less beta-carotene), but same texture and cooking use.

margarine allégée.note: Regular margarine, higher fat content; use a slightly smaller amount.

margarine.note: Light, reduced-fat version, useful for lighter cooking or spreads.

beurre de noisette, pur, sans sucre ajou.note: Smooth almond butter, similar texture and use (spreads, baking), almond flavor instead of hazelnut.

huile de germe de maïs.note: Regular corn oil, almost identical flavor and use.

huile de pistache.note: Walnut oil, another nut oil, different flavor but similar role for dressing and finishing.

huile de noix de pécan.note: Walnut oil, similar nutty aromatic profile, good substitute for dressings and finishing touches.

huile de sésame grillé.note: Regular sesame oil, less toasted and less intense flavor; use slightly more to compensate.

huile de sésame.note: Toasted sesame oil, more intense and roasted flavor; use in smaller amounts.
Black sesame oil, bolder flavor and darker color, for a more pronounced touch.

huile de tournesol vierge, pressée à fro.note: Regular refined sunflower oil, more neutral flavor, suitable both cold and for cooking.

huile de tournesol.note: Cold-pressed virgin version, more pronounced seed flavor, best for raw dressings.

huile de colza vierge, pressée à froid.note: Regular refined rapeseed oil, milder flavor, holds up better to cooking heat.

huile de colza.note: Cold-pressed virgin version, more pronounced nutty flavor, best kept for cold preparations.

suif de mouton.note: Beef fat (tallow), very similar texture and use for frying/baking, slightly milder flavor.

beurre allégé.note: Regular butter, higher fat content; use a slightly smaller amount.

beurre fermier cru, non pasteurisé.note: Regular pasteurized dairy butter, works very well for cooking, with a less farmhouse, fruity flavor.

huile d'olive vierge, non filtrée.note: Filtered extra virgin olive oil, slightly less rustic flavor but comparable quality.

huile de sésame noir.note: Regular sesame oil, lighter color and slightly less bold flavor.

sauce gribiche.note: Regular mayonnaise, ideally enriched with chopped hard-boiled egg and capers to get closer to gribiche.

sauce ravigote.note: Regular vinaigrette with added capers, gherkins and chopped herbs to get closer to ravigote.

sauce mornay.note: Béchamel sauce with added grated cheese, which is exactly the base of a homemade Mornay sauce.

sauce choron.note: Béarnaise sauce with a little added tomato paste, which makes a homemade Choron sauce.

pico de gallo.note: Fresh salsa sauce, very similar texture and use (tacos, grilled meats, eggs).

sauce cranberry (condiment).note: Redcurrant jelly, a tangy condiment traditionally served with poultry and game, a good substitute for cranberry sauce.

gelée de groseille.note: Cranberry sauce, a similar sweet-tart condiment to accompany poultry and game.

piccalilli.nom: Pickles, chowchow, with cauliflower onion mustard, sweet
piccalilli.note: Chowchow (a vinegar-and-mustard vegetable relish), very close to English piccalilli.

chowchow (pickles), au chou-fleur, oigno.note: Piccalilli, an English vegetable relish with mustard and turmeric, very close to chowchow.

sauce meunière.note: Brown butter with added lemon juice and chopped parsley, which recreates a homemade meunière sauce.

sauce colombo, prête à l'emploi.note: Regular curry sauce, less complex flavor (without the specific Caribbean colombo spices) but same use.

sauce chien (antillaise).note: Chimichurri sauce, an herb-and-oil sauce to go with grilled meats, less lemony flavor but similar use.

sauce raita.note: Yogurt-based tzatziki, a yogurt-and-cucumber sauce very close to raita, usually a bit less spiced.

tzatziki à base de yaourt, préemballé.note: Raita sauce, an Indian yogurt-and-cucumber sauce very close to tzatziki, often more spiced.

sauce arrabbiata.note: Regular tomato sauce with added chili (fresh, powdered or flaked) to get closer to arrabbiata.

sauce puttanesca.note: Tomato sauce with added olives, capers and chopped anchovies to get closer to puttanesca.

sauce curry vert thaï.note: Green curry paste to dilute with coconut milk, the classic base for recreating Thai green curry sauce.

sauce curry rouge thaï.note: Red curry paste to dilute with coconut milk, the classic base for recreating Thai red curry sauce.

sauce à l'ail (toum libanais).note: Mayonnaise with crushed garlic added, creamy texture close to toum, but milder.

sauce yakiniku.note: Teriyaki sauce, also sweet-savory and soy-based, a good substitute for marinating or glazing grilled meats.

sauce teriyaki.note: Yakiniku sauce, also sweet-savory and soy-based, a good substitute for teriyaki.

sauce nuoc cham.note: Plain fish sauce (nuoc-mâm), saltier and without the other flavors (lime, sugar, chili); dilute and sweeten slightly.

sauce piri-piri.note: Harissa, a thicker North African chili paste, similar use for spicing up grilled meats and marinades.

sauce zhoug.note: Chimichurri, an herb-and-oil sauce (parsley instead of coriander), similar culinary role for accompanying grilled meats.

sauce enchilada verte.nom: Sauce, enchilada, red, mild, ready to serve
sauce enchilada verte.note: Tomato-based red enchilada sauce, less tangy flavor than the tomatillo version, but same use.

sauce enchilada rouge, douce, prête à se.note: Tomatillo-based green enchilada sauce, tangier, but same use for topping enchiladas.

sauce moutarde au miel.note: Store-bought honey mustard salad dressing, an almost identical product.
